title: TREWS: early sepsis alerts evaluated in five hospitals
summary: A machine-learning system monitored about 590,000 patients in five hospitals, flagging sepsis risk from medical records. In the studied cohort, timely clinical confirmation of alerts was associated with lower mortality, organ failure and length of stay. Observational study: the association does not show that AI caused better outcomes.
organization: Johns Hopkins University; and Bayesian Health

evidence.tested: A prospective multi-site cohort of 590,736 monitored patients (five hospitals) compared outcomes of sepsis alerts confirmed by a provider within 3 hours with outcomes otherwise, adjusting for severity.
evidence.unknown: The association is observational and does not show that the AI caused better outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning early warning system (TREWS) flagged sepsis risk from medical records.
